I found the prior work — and a wrinkle worth flagging first.

**The FamilyFund content doesn't live in this worktree.** I'm currently in a clean worktree on `main`. The actual `websites/` work is sitting **uncommitted** in a *different* worktree (`bridge-cse_01WQeqP4Xktz9qxuq1R8shMR`), never merged. So whatever we do next, we should do it there (or move it here) — otherwise the work fragments across worktrees.

Here's the tree of what exists vs. what the existing spec implies is planned:

```
websites/                                    [uncommitted in worktree …shMR]
├── README.md                          ✓ index — both sites, conventions, status
├── dstrader/
│   └── README.md                      ✓ full content spec (133 lines)
└── familyfund/
    └── README.md                      ✓ content spec (129 lines) — the "first shot"

    ── planned (implied by the spec's 10-section page structure) ──
    ├── (1–3) hero + features + story        → could be index/overview.md
    ├── (4)   screenshots                    → needs synthetic captures, not md
    ├── (5)   architecture / under the hood  → architecture.md (+ ER diagram)
    ├── (6)   integrated platform + thesis   → platform.md (links dstrader)
    ├── (7)   reliability & operations       → operations.md
    ├── (8)   roadmap (AI direction)         → roadmap.md
    └── (9)   about / contact                → about.md
```

**What's actually there today:** the FamilyFund README is a *single* content spec — product one-liner, a 10-section page outline, feature→model mapping, an architecture section, the dstrader integration framing, a redaction checklist, and a candidate stack. It's a complete first draft of the *copy*, all in one file.

So "creating md files to explain the family fund" most naturally means **exploding that one spec into per-page/per-topic markdown files** (the right-hand column above) so each section becomes a real draft you can edit and eventually render.
